method_note: All www.sap.com/design-system URLs return HTTP 403 to WebFetch (reproduced independently this run). Verification was performed by rendering each URL in the in-app browser and running exact-substring matching of each evidence_quote against document.querySelector('main').innerText. Page identity was confirmed via document.title and the breadcrumb line before accepting any extraction. Mid-run the browser pane became corrupted (served unrelated Zoho ERP docs on tabs 9/10 regardless of requested URL); all extractions from those tabs were discarded and re-done on a known-good tab whose rendered breadcrumb matched the requested path. GitHub SAP-docs and legacy help.sap.com records were verified via WebFetch.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Fully responsive tables are the responsive table, list, and tree.'
results.notes: Verbatim match.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Desktop-centric tables are the analytical table, grid table, and tree table. They are optimized for handling a large data sets, but not fully responsive.'
results.notes: Verbatim match.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'When your data is of average complexity, the responsive table can handle up to 200 items.' The 'loaded not stored' qualifier is also explicit: 'the limit is not on the number of items in the database or in the filtered results, but the volume of data loaded at any point.'
results.notes: Both halves of the claim verified on-page.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Use the tree table if: Data needs to be displayed in a hierarchical manner.' It is indeed the only bullet under that heading.
results.notes: The 'single criterion' framing is accurate — one bullet only.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Use the analytical table if: You need multilevel grouping as well as grand totals and subtotals.'
results.notes: Verbatim match.

results.what_source_actually_says: Limitations list: 'Only one control can be added per cell. It supports only single-row templates. All items need to have the same height.' All three sub-claims present.
results.notes: Verbatim match.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Vertical scrolling is not smooth. For performance reasons, the content is not really scrolled but exchanged.'
results.notes: Verbatim match; the 'exchanged not scrolled' rationale is on-page.

results.replacement_quote: You can add any number of line items to the tree table, which uses "lazy loading". ... The tree table is optimized to allow faster scrolling within the first 1000 items.
results.what_source_actually_says: SAP states a SCROLL-PERFORMANCE OPTIMISATION WINDOW, not a capacity limit. Immediately before the 1000-item sentence the same section says: 'You can add any number of line items to the tree table, which uses "lazy loading".' SAP nowhere calls 1000 a boundary, maximum, or limit for the tree table, and states no maximum node count anywhere on the page.
results.notes: MOST IMPORTANT FINDING. The evidence_quote matched verbatim, but the claim recasts it as 'the documented performance boundary for hierarchy screens' and the record escalates it to 'HARD CONSTRAINT: the WBS workbench must keep the expanded node count near or under 1000'. That is not what the source supports. Narrower true statement: scrolling is optimised to be faster within the first 1000 items; beyond that scrolling is still supported (unlimited rows via lazy loading) but not in the optimised fast-scroll window. Note the sibling record R09-021 states the SAME SAP sentence correctly (it includes the unlimited-rows clause), so the lane is internally inconsistent about the identical fact. Collapsed defaults and lazy child loading remain good design, but they cannot be justified as an SAP-documented hard limit.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Ideally, you should only show trees with a lot of hierarchical data as a last resort. Try the following instead: Break down the data into manageable chunks and allow the user to navigate or drill down between them. Use charts with drilldown functionality...'
results.notes: Both alternatives named in the claim are on-page. Source hedges with 'Ideally'.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'A tree table is available for desktops and tablets, but not in smartphone sizes. ... For smartphones, you need to take an adaptive approach by offering an additional UI.'
results.notes: Verbatim match; the 'separate adaptive UI' half is also explicit.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'The tree column is always the first column and cannot be dragged.'
results.notes: Verbatim. Additional nuance for the build: 'If the tree column is hidden, the following column is the tree column' — i.e. the pin follows the tree role, not a fixed field.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'The Freeze/Unfreeze option is provided in the column header menu of all columns. Using Freeze on one column freezes all columns from the first one to the selected one.'
results.notes: Verbatim match, BUT the same page contradicts itself: its 'Column Header Menu' component section states 'For the tree column, the column header menu can contain the menu item Freeze and a Filter field... For all other columns, only the free text filter is available.' SAP's own page is inconsistent about whether Freeze appears on all columns or only the tree column. Flagged because the record drives an implementation decision.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'To prevent adverse side effects when scrolling vertically, all line items must have the same height.' Same statement independently present on the grid-table page and in the table-overview limitations list.
results.notes: Claim's scope ('tree and grid tables') verified on both pages.

results.what_source_actually_says: Developer Hint: 'The tree table itself has no influence on the filter result. It sends a filter request and displays whatever comes back. Make sure that the result set is meaningful.'
results.notes: Verbatim match.

results.replacement_quote: For many trees, the following approach works well if you want to apply filters only to the leaves of a tree: Remove all leaves that don't fit the filter criteria. Remove empty nodes.
results.what_source_actually_says: SAP presents this as a CONDITIONAL heuristic, not a universal recommendation: it is prefaced 'For many trees, the following approach works well IF you want to apply filters only to the leaves of a tree'. The page then explicitly addresses the other case: 'Where nodes need to be filtered, keep the following in mind: A node may or may not fit the filter criteria. A node can contain items (nodes and/or leaves) that fit the filter criteria. Because of this, the results might contain more nodes than those that are relevant for the filter criteria.'
results.notes: Quote matched verbatim but the claim drops the governing condition and the record asserts it 'defines the WBS filter algorithm precisely'. If WBS nodes themselves carry filterable attributes (status, owner, cost centre) — which they do — the leaf-only algorithm is the wrong one. Materially affects the filter design.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'If sorting is meaningful, is it meaningful on all levels? Or does the tree structure need to be stable? In the latter case, sort only leaves, but not nodes.'
results.notes: Verbatim; conditional ('where structure must stay stable') is correctly preserved in the claim.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'If your structure contains many items on the root level, it might make sense to collapse the whole tree in the beginning. In contrast, if the main items to work with are displayed on a deeper level... the tree should be expanded up to the first level where the needed items appear.'
results.notes: Verbatim. Note the record's applicability ('open collapsed to level 2') leans on R09-008's overstated 1000-item constraint; the initial-depth advice itself is sound and source-backed.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'We strongly recommend using the multi-selection plug-in. This ensures that all items selected using Select All or as part of a range are included – even if some items were not initially loaded in the front end. This is not the case if you use the multi-toggle option.'
results.notes: Verbatim. Implementation nuance worth carrying: with the plug-in, 'By default, a dedicated Deselect All button replaces the Select All checkbox. There is no default UI element for selecting all items' unless limit=0.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'The range that can be selected using the Shift key is limited to the specified number of items (default = 200).' Identical wording on the tree-table and analytical-table pages.
results.notes: Scope note: this limit is a property of sap.ui.table.plugins.MultiSelectionPlugin only. In plain multi-toggle mode there is no such cap. Since R09-018 adopts the plug-in, the claim holds for our configuration.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Selecting this checkbox selects or deselects all items that are currently loaded in the front end (keyboard: CTRL+A). All other items are not selected/deselected. If the application data is stored in the back end, scrolling down further can reveal additional unselected items.'
results.notes: Verbatim; the 'later-loaded rows appear unselected' half is explicit.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'You can add any number of line items to the grid table, which uses "lazy loading". ... The grid table is optimized to allow faster scrolling within the first 1000 items.'
results.notes: Correctly framed — this record pairs the 1000-item fast-scroll window with the unlimited-rows clause. Contrast with R09-008, which drops that clause and calls the same fact a boundary.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Use the analytical table (ALV) if: ... You have to work on more than 1,000 rows. In this case, the analytical table is easier to handle.'
results.notes: Verbatim match.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'You cannot provide an analytical binding on the technical side. In this case, a grid table will do the work. However, please note that the grid table doesn't provide grouping, aggregation options, and is not responsive.' Corroborated by the table-overview Developer Hint: 'The analytical table needs analytical binding.'
results.notes: Verbatim; both clauses verified.

results.replacement_quote: Data needs to be structured in a hierarchical manner. In this case, a tree table might be more appropriate. Although the analytical table can have several grouping levels, it is not as flexible when nodes at several levels contain children.
results.what_source_actually_says: The claim is true and directly supported — but by a DIFFERENT passage than the one cited. The cited string 'Several grouping levels are possible.' does occur on the page (character offset ~15582) yet it sits in the Grouping mechanics section describing group-header formatting, and carries none of the analytical-vs-tree comparison the claim makes. The supporting text is in the 'Do not use the analytical table if' list at offset ~3369.
results.notes: Textual match was coincidental. Cite the replacement quote instead — it is the sentence that actually licenses 'do not model WBS parentage as grouping columns'.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Table personalization can be applied to simple tables (up to about 20 columns) and complex tables (more than about 20 columns) using different controls.' View settings dialog: 'fewer than about 20 columns'. P13n dialog: 'You are using an analytical table (ALV). The user is able to personalize more than about 20 columns. Complex queries have to be built.'
results.notes: Verbatim. Minor addition: use of an analytical table triggers P13n regardless of column count.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'The table personalization dialog can show/hide and reorder columns.' and 'Use the view settings dialog if: ... A combination of sorting, filtering, and grouping is needed.'
results.notes: Both halves of the split verified.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'All table personalization dialogs are opened via the Settings button on the right-hand side of the table toolbar.' Independently corroborated on the table-personalization-dialog page.
results.notes: Verbatim match.

results.what_source_actually_says: Under 'Do not use table personalization at all if:' — 'A very complex filter is needed. In this case, consider using a filter bar instead of the filter tab.'
results.notes: Verbatim match.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Note on terminology: On the user interface, we now call variants "views", which is better understood by end users. To describe the SAPUI5 controls, however, we still speak of "variants" and "variant management".'
results.notes: Verbatim; both halves explicit.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'There can only be one default view, which the user can change in the Manage Views dialog. If the user sets a new default view, the last view remains as a favorite.'
results.notes: Verbatim match.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Public views are visible to all users who have access to the app. A view can be set to Public by individual users, key users, SAP (default delivery), or partners. ... A public view can be edited by the user who created it and by key users. All other users can only display the public view.'
results.notes: Verbatim; the creator+key-user edit rule is explicit, supporting the owner_id / is_public / admin-override model.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'The standard view is the minimum set of filters delivered by SAP, and cannot be modified or deleted. It is flagged as a favorite and cannot be removed. There can be several pre-shipped standard views, depending on the use case.'
results.notes: Verbatim. Minor: SAP allows SEVERAL pre-shipped standard views; the claim's singular phrasing is a simplification, not an error.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Apply Automatically: If checked, the view is applied immediately whenever it is selected. The user does not need to click the Go button in the filter bar. We do not recommend checking this option if the selection is likely to cause long loading times.'
results.notes: Verbatim; the 'discouraged for long loading times' half is explicit.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'If the user has made changes to the user interface that affect the saved view, the view is marked with an asterisk (*) to indicate the unsaved changes.'
results.notes: Verbatim match.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'If you use variants, we recommend using one variant management control for the whole page. Use the variants to save and restore all settings for filters, selected tabs, all tables, and all charts. In some specific cases, you might need to add a second variant at control level... However, the default is to use a single variant management control for the entire page.'
results.notes: Verbatim; payload scope and exception status both explicit.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'An asterisk next to the filter label indicates the filter is mandatory.' Related: 'For list reports and overview pages, preset values for mandatory filters to prevent error messages when the page loads.'
results.notes: Verbatim. The 'must carry values for the search to return results' half is supported indirectly via the preset-to-avoid-errors guidance rather than stated literally.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Next to Adapt Filters, the number of active filters is displayed in parentheses. A filter is active when a value is assigned to it either in the filter bar or the Adapt Filters dialog. Note that a filter can be active, but not visible in the filter bar.'
results.notes: Verbatim; the hidden-but-active nuance is explicit.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Whenever possible, use the live update mode because it is more convenient for the user. Consider the manual update mode only in cases where: The volume of unfiltered data to load would be excessively high. The users need to enter multiple filter values...'
results.notes: Verbatim; the named exceptions justify the record's 'Go button for expensive roll-ups' conclusion.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Use the basic search field to provide a keyword search. Do not show a search field in the table toolbar.'
results.notes: Verbatim; both halves adjacent on-page.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Use the value help dialog if: ... The user needs to define conditions, such as ranges and exclusions.' The select-dialog page independently supplies the comparison: 'A more enhanced dialog for single selection and multiselection is the value help dialog as it offers range selection and excluding functions.'
results.notes: Verbatim. The cited page never names the select dialog; the 'chosen over the select dialog' framing is corroborated on the select-dialog page instead.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'The selected items and conditions are displayed in a tokenizer... Each selected item or condition is displayed as one token. There is no longer a visual difference between included and excluded items and conditions. They are now differentiated using operators.'
results.notes: Verbatim. Slight precision note: SAP says 'no longer a visual difference', not specifically 'rather than colour'.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'The select dialog enables users to select one or more items from a comprehensive list. The select dialog comes with a list of entries and a search field to filter the list.'
results.notes: Verbatim match.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'SAP Fiori has five semantic colors, which are associated with the following predefined value states: Regular (neutral), Good (positive), Warning (critical), Bad (error), Information (highlight).' Separately: 'There is no predefined meaning for the individual colors in the generic palette.'
results.notes: Verbatim; both the five-colour set and the meaningless-industry-palette half verified.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'In addition to using a color, you must also provide a text, such as an object status. All colors require a corresponding descriptive text for accessibility purposes.'
results.notes: Verbatim. The record's 'HARD RULE' escalation is justified — SAP uses 'must'.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'The indication color palette is supported exclusively by tables and the object status.' And under 'No Palette Mix': 'you can only use one color palette at a time. It is not possible to mix different colors from both palettes.'
results.notes: Verbatim; both halves verified.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Object status: a short text that represents the semantic status of an object.' Plus 'An optional icon (property: icon)' and 'Note that there is no generic icon for "neutral" across industries. If you have a neutral object status, use the text-only version, or a blank icon.'
results.notes: All three sub-claims verified (initial needle for 'neutral icon' failed only because SAP words it 'no generic icon for "neutral"').

results.verifier_http_status: 200 (browser render; canonical path is .../interaction/states/interaction-foundations-value-states, cited URL resolves)
results.what_source_actually_says: 'A UI element can have only one value state at any given time. By default, the value states are depicted using the standard semantic colors for the respective theme (such as Morning Horizon).' Available states: None, Positive, Negative, Warning, Information, Custom.
results.notes: Verbatim. Useful addition for the record's 'precedence order' need: the semantic-colors page defines a Color Hierarchy — 'the overall color is based on the color hierarchy: colors higher up in the hierarchy take precedence' — so the precedence rule is documented, not something we must invent.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Mass editing allows users to simultaneously change multiple objects that share the same editable properties.' 'Mass editing is done in a dialog containing combo boxes and select controls.' 'Users will typically select multiple objects from a list or table and press the Edit button.'
results.notes: Verbatim; all elements of the claim verified.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'If the values are different, < Keep Values >. If the values are all identical, that specific value is preselected. If a column contains no existing values, the option < Leave Blank > is preselected. If it's technically possible, the option < Clear Values > is available in the dropdown list to remove all the values in a column.' '< Keep Existing Values >' also appears in the combo-box preset table.
results.notes: Verbatim. The tri-state semantics the record depends on are actually four-state: Keep Values / specific value / Leave Blank / Clear Values. Worth widening the bulk-update payload design accordingly.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'All micro charts are fully responsive. The size of the control adapts automatically to the size of the parent container and does not have a defined width or height.'
results.notes: First half verbatim on the cited page. SOURCING NOTE: the second half of the claim (only XS bullet/comparison/stacked-bar permitted in grid and tree table cells) is NOT on the micro-chart page — 'grid table' does not appear there at all. It is independently verified on the tree-table and grid-table pages, both of which list cell contents including 'The following micro charts in size XS: Bullet, comparison, stacked bar'. Claim is true; re-point the citation for the second clause.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Keep in mind that the bullet micro chart shows data points for given points in time. Do not use it to show a time series.' Time-series alternatives named: line, column micro charts.
results.notes: Verbatim match.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'The file size of the exported file is limited by the available browser memory. Exporting large tables can therefore lead to memory overflows and browser crashes. The recommended maximum table size is 1 million table cells for desktop browsers or 100,000 table cells on tablets and phones. For larger tables, consider using custom-built, specialized export solutions instead.'
results.notes: Verbatim. MISSED DETAIL WORTH ADDING: SAP gives hard numbers (1,000,000 cells desktop / 100,000 cells tablet-phone) that the record omits. These are directly usable as the WBS export cutover threshold.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Since spreadsheet applications provide their own formatting for cell content, SAPUI5 formatters (for example, for dates, times, and numbers) are not taken into account.' And: 'To ensure that the data is exported as it is displayed on the screen, you can define key value pairs to overwrite the back-end values for a given column or columns (such as "F" for "Finished"). ... The correct translated text must be provided by the application. It isn't done by the framework.'
results.notes: Verbatim; the key-value-pair mechanism is explicit (SAP writes 'key value pairs', unhyphenated).

results.what_source_actually_says: 'In the spreadsheet files, tree structures are displayed using the grouping functionality (first seven levels) and double indentation (all levels).'
results.notes: Verbatim match.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Empty states can be handled by the illustrated message control.' And: 'It is important to tell the user what the empty state is for, why the user is seeing it, and what the user can do next.' Types listed include No data and User action (no search results / no filter results).
results.notes: Verbatim; the three-part guidance and the distinct empty-state categories both verified.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Try to avoid empty tables. If necessary, provide instructions on how to fill the tree table with data. Remove the item count in the table title if there are zero items.' Same rule on the grid-table page.
results.notes: Verbatim; all three sub-claims present.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Do not use the busy dialog for app or page loading. Set the busy state at app level.' Also 'Do not use the busy dialog to block the entire UI. Otherwise, this would also affect the shell bar' and 'Separate busy states for list and detail areas'.
results.notes: Verbatim. The record's requirement for independent tree/detail busy states is directly modelled on-page.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Visually, skeleton pages are grey boxes with animations to indicate loading activity.' And: 'for each floorplan there is a generic placeholder that is displayed as a generic fixed page.'
results.notes: Verbatim; the per-floorplan half also verified.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'To indicate that the tree table contains items with errors or warnings, show a message strip above the tree table. On the message strip, provide information on errors or warnings. When issues are solved or when new issues appear, update the message strip accordingly.'
results.notes: Verbatim; the 'kept updated' half is explicit.

results.verifier_http_status: NAV_FAILED (repeated); no keyboard page exists in the interaction foundations index
results.what_source_actually_says: Could not be retrieved. The cited URL failed to load on every attempt (5 tries, two tabs, with and without trailing slash). Crucially, the v1-136 Interaction Design Foundations overview page enumerates every child article via in-page links, and the complete list is: cursors, drag-and-drop (overview/reorder/resize/move/data-transfer), gestures, motion-design, states (component/focus/interaction/selection/value/state-combinations), wrapping-and-truncation. There is NO keyboard-support page and no screen-reader page in that section.
results.notes: Cannot confirm the quote 'Every application and UI component must be fully operable using the keyboard.' A targeted WebSearch of sap.com returned only differently-worded statements. The underlying principle is near-certainly SAP policy, but per the tier gate an unfetchable page cannot yield CONFIRMED. Do not cite this sentence as a verbatim SAP quote downstream.

results.what_source_actually_says: Not retrievable. The cited v1-148 accessibility product-standard URL alternately returned a navigation failure and SAP's own 'Sorry, this page can't be found' 404 body across ~6 attempts, three tabs, and with/without trailing slash. The v1-136 and v1-120 equivalents also failed.
results.notes: The Ctrl-L keyboard-capture exception could not be re-verified. This directly affects the record's conclusion that 'We can safely bind Ctrl+S, Ctrl+Enter etc.' — do not treat the shortcut namespace as cleared until this page is re-read.

results.what_source_actually_says: Resize: 'The width of the focused column header can be increased with Shift+Right and decreased with Shift+Left.' Reorder (Rearrange Columns section): 'the focused column header can be moved by one position to the corresponding direction with Ctrl+Left / Ctrl+Right.'
results.notes: Quote verbatim and the Ctrl+arrow reorder binding is confirmed. HOWEVER the same page contradicts itself: its earlier Column Header component section says columns 'can be moved by one position to the corresponding direction with Shift+Left / Shift+Right'. Since the record's value is 'concrete keybindings to implement', flag that SAP's page gives two different reorder chords; the grid-table and analytical-table pages both say Ctrl+Left/Ctrl+Right, so Ctrl is the better-supported reading.

results.replacement_quote: Morning Horizon — WCAG 2.2 AA; Evening Horizon — WCAG 2.2 AA; Horizon High Contrast Black — WCAG 2.2 AAA; Horizon High Contrast White — WCAG 2.2 AAA; Quartz Light — WCAG 2.1 AA; Quartz Dark — WCAG 2.1 AA. (source: /v1-148/foundations/visual/theming, Accessibility section)
results.what_source_actually_says: The cited accessibility page is unreachable, so the quote is unverified. BUT the record's attached caveat — 'the explicit level letter was NOT found on this page' / 'SAP does not state a conformance level' — is CONTRADICTED by a different v1-148 Tier-1 page that this same lane already cites twice (R09-067, R09-068): /foundations/visual/theming states per-theme WCAG target versions INCLUDING levels, in a table: 'SAP visual themes follow the WCAG target version that was valid at the time of the theme release' — Morning Horizon WCAG 2.2 AA, Horizon HCB/HCW WCAG 2.2 AAA, Quartz Light/Dark WCAG 2.1 AA. It adds: 'Please make sure you choose the appropriate theme if you need to support a specific WCAG policy in your company or organization.'
results.notes: See contradictions[]. The lane's declared gap on conformance level is closeable from a page already in the lane's own search_log.

results.what_source_actually_says: Not retrievable; the 7:1 figure could not be re-verified. The string '7:1' does not appear on the theming page. Adjacent verifiable fact: the theming page assigns Horizon High Contrast Black/White a WCAG 2.2 AAA target, and AAA is the level at which 7:1 text contrast is required — consistent with the claim but an inference, not a quote.
results.notes: The existence of user-selectable high-contrast themes IS independently confirmed on the theming page (High Contrast Black (HCB) and High Contrast White (HCW) listed as shipped themes). Only the 7:1 figure and the 'persisted as a preference' detail remain unverified.

results.what_source_actually_says: Not retrievable. A sap.com-scoped WebSearch surfaced closely matching prose ('The SAPUI5 framework is technically prepared for screen reader support... However, the actual structure, as well as the actual visible and invisible texts, need to be defined at application level'), but a search-engine summary is Tier 3 and cannot raise this above UNVERIFIED.
results.notes: The design conclusion (budget explicit ARIA labelling work) is sound engineering regardless, but the sentence must not be quoted as verified SAP text.

results.verifier_http_status: 404 (SAP 'Sorry, this page can't be found' body rendered)
results.what_source_actually_says: The URL returns SAP's own 404 page (main content length 130 chars: 'Sorry, this page can't be found. Use the search bar at the top of the page or browse using the link below.'). Confirmed structurally: the Interaction Design Foundations overview page's link list contains no screen-reader entry.
results.notes: Definite negative — this is not a transient failure, the cited page does not exist at this path. The unique-labels requirement could not be verified anywhere in the design-system this run.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'The latest theme for SAP applications is called Morning Horizon. In addition, SAP provides alternative themes: Evening Horizon as an optional dark theme and also Quartz Light, Quartz Dark and the accessibility themes High-Contrast Black (HCB) and High-Contrast White (HCW).'
results.notes: Verbatim; all named themes verified. IP discipline respected — no colour values recorded.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'All of the user interface components are specified using cross-technology design tokens that are mapped 1:1 with theming variables provided in multiple formats in the SAP theming base content. Theming variables come in the form of CSS variables, LESS, SASS, and JSON.'
results.notes: Verbatim. The claim's 'one-to-one' renders SAP's '1:1'; all four formats match exactly.

results.what_source_actually_says: Not retrievable at the cited URL. I additionally searched the theming page (the natural alternative home for this guidance) for 'Change individual colors only in exceptional cases' and for 'exceptional cases' — both NOT FOUND there. So the sentence is not recoverable from the pages reachable this run.
results.notes: The 'tokens only, no hard-coded colours' build rule is well supported by the CONFIRMED R09-068 token architecture, so the design conclusion survives even though this specific warning is unverified.

results.replacement_quote: Texts are left-aligned. Numbers (except for IDs), dates, and times are right-aligned. Icons are centered. Micro charts are left-aligned. (source: /v1-148/ui-elements/tree-table/usage, 'Alignment of Cell Content')
results.what_source_actually_says: The quote matched verbatim, but the cited page scopes itself explicitly AGAINST the control family this record feeds. Its Usage section states: 'Do not use this cheat sheet if: You need to design content for a list, tree, grid table, analytical table, or tree table.' The record nonetheless feeds 'wbs-workbench-ui', which is a TREE TABLE. The tree table has its own, slightly different alignment rule (replacement_quote): it does not mention phone numbers, URLs, passwords or email addresses, and it adds centred icons and left-aligned micro charts.
results.notes: Narrower true statement: the phone-number/URL/password/email alignment specifics are responsive-table guidance only. For the WBS grid, cite the tree-table alignment rule instead. The record's practical conclusion (WBS code left, cost and dates right) still holds under BOTH rules — WBS codes are IDs, and IDs are left-aligned in each.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'The absolute date formats shown below are based on the Unicode Common Locale Data Repository (CLDR).' 'In general, use the medium date format.' 'The formatting and order of the values differ based on the locale settings that have been configured in the browser.'
results.notes: Verbatim; all three components of the claim verified. Caveat on-page: on ABAP web application servers the short and medium CLDR patterns are replaced by ABAP user patterns.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'If you need to display date intervals, use an en dash "–" (not a minus sign) as a delimiter between the dates. For example, Feb 16, 2016 – Feb 18, 2016'
results.notes: Verbatim match.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'You can use four different data types for numbers: integer, float, currency, and percentage. Each data type can be formatted using a short, standard, or long format.' And: 'In general, use standard format.'
results.notes: Verbatim; all four types and the standard-format recommendation verified. Also on-page: 'Do not use number formatting if: You need to display IDs. You need to display telephone numbers.'

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Most currencies have two decimal places, although some need three digits after the decimal point, such as the Tunisian dinar. The currency formatter takes this into account. Currency amounts are rounded down automatically.'
results.notes: Verbatim; both the three-decimal handling and the round-down behaviour verified. The record's guard (display rounding must never write back to stored WBS cost) is a sound inference, not an SAP statement.

results.verifier_http_status: 200 (via raw.githubusercontent.com equivalent of the cited blob)
results.what_source_actually_says: 'SAPUI5 sets the RTL mode based on the current language which is usually picked automatically based on the locale configuration of the user's browser or profile data.' 'The default text direction is left-to-right (LTR).' Configuration: 'URL parameter sap-ui-rtl=true'.
results.notes: All three components of the claim verified in the canonical SAP-docs repo.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Changing the directionality has a big impact on text-displaying controls, images and the alignment of the whole application.' And: 'Self-written controls and content has to be tested separately. If you require manual styles, provide a style specifically for the RTL case by using html[dir=rtl].'
results.notes: Verbatim; both halves verified. Legacy static help.sap.com route worked exactly as the routing note predicted. Note the lane's own gap entry correctly flags that the tree-indentation/chevron mirroring conclusion is OUR inference, not an SAP design rule.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'textDirection adds an HTML dir attribute to the part of the control that displays the target content.' 'textAlign ... is used for reversing the text alignment.' 'This common pitfall is visible when representing numerals (phone numbers, dates, currency values, etc.), which actually need to be displayed in LTR mode within the context of an RTL page.'
results.notes: Verbatim; the LTR-islands requirement is explicit, supporting the WBS-code-as-LTR-island conclusion.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'To show more than 100 items, use the "growing" mode... You decide whether the user triggers the request by scrolling (preferred) or by clicking the More button.'
results.notes: Verbatim; the scroll-preferred-over-More-button ordering is explicit.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Don't show aggregations in "growing" mode. In "growing" mode it isn't clear which values are being aggregated; only the items currently loaded in the front end, or all items.'
results.notes: Verbatim; the stated rationale matches the claim exactly. Strong support for server-side WBS totals.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'The default minimum width per column is 8 rem. You can change this value for each column... Low-priority columns move to the pop-in area first (right-most low priority column first), medium-priority columns next, and high-priority columns last. The default priority is "none", which is handled like the "medium" priority.'
results.notes: Verbatim; both halves verified, and the default priority ('none' behaving as medium) is a useful addition.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'When the user scrolls, the title bar, column headers, and filter infobar can stick to the top of the surrounding layout container (sap.m.Table, property: sticky).'
results.notes: Verbatim. Caveat the record omits: SAP lists real limitations — 'It is not available on all browsers' and 'Certain layout containers suppress the sticky behavior, such as the grid layout. The same happens if the table is placed within the object page.' Temper the record's 'Mandatory for a deep WBS list' accordingly.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'The table toolbar always appears above the table. Use it for key actions that affect the entire table and for actions that apply to selected items.' Anatomy confirms grouping and separators; Top Tips: 'Keep the predefined order for action groups.'
results.notes: Verbatim; all three components of the claim verified.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'You can add an item counter after the title. The counter shows the number of items displayed in the table in parentheses, for example, (37). Remove the counter when no items are shown.'
results.notes: Verbatim for the item counter. The claim's trailing 'selection can be surfaced alongside it' is weakly supported here; the selected-item count is documented on the infobar page (R09-086) rather than in the table title.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'In tables, a variant stores all the settings that define the table view, such as the column layout, column visibility, sorting, filter settings, and grouping.' And: 'In most cases, variant management replaces the title.'
results.notes: Verbatim; the exact five-part payload the record needs as its saved-view schema is enumerated on-page. Note SAP writes 'such as', so the list is illustrative rather than closed.

results.what_source_actually_says: Top Tips: 'Include only the actions and content your users really need. Keep the predefined order for action groups. Don't move main actions into the overflow.'
results.notes: Verbatim; both halves adjacent on-page.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'The infobar is a type of toolbar that appears above a list or panel, and shows filter or selection settings: Filter criteria... Do not show the infobar if no filter is applied. Selected items: In a multi-select dialog, the infobar shows the number of selected items.'
results.notes: Verbatim. Two scope precisions: SAP says 'above a list or panel' (not specifically 'above the table'), and the selected-item count is documented for a MULTI-SELECT DIALOG specifically.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'The smart table creates a responsive table, grid table, tree table, or analytical table based on an OData (Open Data Protocol) service and its annotations. The table toolbar comes with additional built-in features, such as personalization, export to spreadsheet, and variant management.'
results.notes: Verbatim; all elements verified. Constraint the record omits: 'You use an OData service for your app (OData version 2 only)' — relevant if the single-configurable-table argument is carried into a non-OData Zoho backend.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Variant management is optional... Guidelines: Use variant management only if really needed.'
results.notes: Verbatim match.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Do not use the flexible column layout if: You want to build a workbench or tools layout. The flexible column layout is not meant to provide a main column with additional side columns on the left and/or right. If you want to display additional content to enrich the main content and to help users better perform their tasks, use the dynamic side content instead.'
results.notes: Verbatim, under an explicit 'Do not use' heading, with the dynamic-side-content redirect stated. The HARD CONSTRAINT label is fully earned here — this is the strongest-evidenced record in the lane. Independently corroborated by Tier-2 R09-106.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'The compact factor reduces the size of components, so you can display more information on the UI. Use this factor for devices operated with a mouse and keyboard.' 'All SAP Fiori components support both cozy and compact content density modes. Most components default to cozy.' 'Set the content density based on the user's device capabilities.'
results.notes: Verbatim; all three components verified. Note 'condensed' does not appear on this page (it is documented on the tree/grid/analytical table pages), so the record's own_words mention of a third scale is sourced elsewhere.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Note that the condensed content density has always to be set in addition to compact. Do not use condensed on its own. Do not mix condensed with cozy. Doing so could lead to unpredictable and / or unwanted results, e.g. cozy sized controls in condensed sized containers, missing paddings, etc.'
results.notes: Verbatim; identical wording also on the grid-table and analytical-table pages.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Note that neither compact mode nor condensed mode can be interacted with touch. Even on a desktop with a touch screen, users will have difficulty selecting rows or using controls inside the cells when using their fingers.'
results.notes: Verbatim; the touchscreen-desktop caveat is explicit, supporting the record's touch-detection requirement.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Do not use the status indicator if: You need to display a single value within a table. Use the progress indicator or radial micro chart instead.'
results.notes: Verbatim; the in-table prohibition and both named substitutes verified.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Use the table personalization dialog if: You have small tables. You have a manageable number of columns.' 'The header displays the dialog title and the Reset button to revert to the initial state.' 'The toolbar displays the Move Column Up and Move Column Down buttons, and the Search field.' 'The list header displays the Select All checkbox for selecting all columns.'
results.notes: Verbatim; every element of the claimed anatomy verified.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Row: An item is selected by clicking the checkbox or the row. Use this option... if clicking a row or a cell is not used for anything else. RowSelector: An item is selected only by clicking the checkbox in the selector cell. Use this option if clicking the row (or a cell inside the row) is used for something else, such as navigation. RowOnly: An item is selected only by clicking the row...'
results.notes: Verbatim; all three modes and the navigation-conflict decision rule verified, directly supporting checkbox-only selection for navigable WBS rows.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Never disable the selection checkbox. If an action can't be performed on a specific item, inform the user after the corresponding action has been triggered.'
results.notes: Verbatim; both halves adjacent. Same rule repeated on the grid-table page.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'If nothing is selected, add the new item to the root. If a single node is selected, add the new item to the selected node. If a single leaf is selected, add the new item as child of this leaf. The original selected item becomes a node.' Also: 'Disable Create or Add if more than one item is selected.'
results.notes: Verbatim; all three insertion rules plus the leaf-becomes-node transition verified. The multi-selection disable rule is a useful addition the record omits.

results.what_source_actually_says: Three options in priority order: '1. Add the item inline... recommended for simple scenarios with just a few columns. 2. Open a dialog for larger tree tables with up to 8 editable columns. 3. Navigate to a new page... for very complex scenarios that cannot be handled by a dialog (for example, tree tables with more than 8 columns).'
results.notes: Verbatim; the escalation ladder and the 8-column switch point verified exactly as claimed.

results.what_source_actually_says: Three states New / Recent / Added are defined. Recent: 'keep the item highlighted and display it as the first item of the corresponding node. Ignore current sort, filter, and grouping criteria to keep the item visible.' Added: 'It follows the sort, filter, and grouping settings and also loses the visual highlight.'
results.notes: Verbatim; the state machine described in the claim matches the page precisely.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Enable the shortcut Ctrl+Enter (and ideally Enter in addition) to trigger the Add or Create button.'
results.notes: Verbatim match.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Context menus are opened by right-clicking (desktop), long press (mobile), the context menu key, or Shift+F10.' And: 'Be aware that using the context menu overrides the browser context menu, which can no longer be opened.'
results.notes: Verbatim; all four triggers plus the browser-menu override verified. Caution the record omits: 'Do not combine context menus with condensed mode' — relevant since the record elsewhere proposes a condensed WBS view.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'One or several items can be repositioned within a table or moved to other UI elements using drag and drop operations.' 'Drop targets can be on items, between items, or both.' Guidelines make the semantics explicit: 'For dropping items as a child, use whole nodes as drop targets (DropPosition.On). For dropping items on the same level, use the space between items as drop targets (DropPosition.Between).'
results.notes: Verbatim; the on-node=reparent / between=resequence mapping the record relies on is stated outright. Important companion rule the record omits: 'provide it only in addition to existing (and visible) UI elements' because 'there is no generic keyboard interaction' for drag and drop.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'If all column widths are set in percentage or "auto", resizing one column might also lead to the automatic resizing of some or all other columns. The position of the resized column might also be affected.' Versus: 'If column widths are set in pixel-based units (px, em, rem), the corresponding column is adapted and following columns are moved accordingly. The width of all other columns is not affected.'
results.notes: Verbatim (partial-sentence quote); the pixel-vs-percentage contrast the claim draws is accurate.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Sort status information by the severity of the status: Ascending: Sort status information from positive to negative, with neutral last. Descending: Sort status information from negative to positive, with neutral first.' Also: 'The descending sort order must always be the exact reverse of the ascending sort order.'
results.notes: Verbatim; the 'exact reverse' requirement in the claim is separately stated on-page.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Provide a split menu button for triggering the export... The export icon starts the export with default settings... The dropdown arrow opens a menu with two options: Export... Export As… Opens a dialog for specifying the export settings. ... For Export As…, use the shortcut: Shift+Ctrl+E'
results.notes: Verbatim; the split-menu-button anatomy and the shortcut both verified.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Use the flexible-column layout if you want to create a master-detail or master-detail-detail scenario in which the user can drill down or navigate.' The same page lists among do-not-use cases: 'Build a workbench or tools layout with side columns.'
results.notes: Tier 2 is permitted to reach CONFIRMED for behaviour/UX claims, which this is. Corroborates R09-089 from a second first-party surface, including the workbench exclusion.

results.what_source_actually_says: Independently reproduced this run: WebFetch on the cited v1-136 URL returned 'The server returned HTTP 403 Forbidden.' WebFetch on the v1-148 table-overview URL returned the same 403, while the in-app browser rendered that identical URL in full.
results.notes: Methodological claim, fully reproduced. One correction to the record's own_words: the page-manifest route it recommends (/edge/design-system/fiori-design-web/query-index.json) is NOT reliably usable — WebFetch gets 403 on it, and loading it in the browser hung the tab for 300s and corrupted the browser pane state for the rest of the session. Recommend future lanes drive URLs from in-page link lists (e.g. a section overview page's anchors) rather than the query-index.

contradictions.target: R09 gaps[0] — 'ACCESSIBILITY CONFORMANCE LEVEL' and the note attached to R09-063
contradictions.lane_asserts: SAP's Fiori accessibility product-standard page names WCAG 2.2 as the reference standard but does NOT state a conformance level (A/AA/AAA). 'No first-party level statement located. Do not assert SAP Fiori is WCAG 2.2 AA conformant downstream without a VPAT citation.' R09-063 adds: 'NOTE: the explicit level letter was NOT found on this page.'
contradictions.source_actually_says: A first-party v1-148 page states conformance LEVELS explicitly, per theme, in a table. https://www.sap.com/design-system/fiori-design-web/v1-148/foundations/visual/theming — Accessibility section: 'all SAP's visual themes have been aligned with Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) and follow the recommendations for the Perceivable principle. SAP visual themes follow the WCAG target version that was valid at the time of the theme release.' Table: Morning Horizon = WCAG 2.2 AA; Evening Horizon = WCAG 2.2 AA; Horizon High Contrast Black = WCAG 2.2 AAA; Horizon High Contrast White = WCAG 2.2 AAA; Quartz Light = WCAG 2.1 AA; Quartz Dark = WCAG 2.1 AA; Quartz HCB/HCW = WCAG 2.1 AAA; Belize = WCAG 2.0 AA. Guideline: 'Please make sure you choose the appropriate theme if you need to support a specific WCAG policy in your company or organization.'
contradictions.why_it_matters: The lane closed this as an unfillable gap and instructed downstream authors not to assert a level. The level IS first-party documented — on a page the lane already cites twice (R09-067, R09-068 both use this exact URL), so it was fetched and the Accessibility section simply was not read. The blueprint can now state a defensible target ('WCAG 2.2 AA, matching the Morning Horizon target') with a Tier-1 citation. Precision required: SAP frames these as per-theme TARGET VERSIONS for visual themes, which is a narrower claim than 'SAP Fiori is WCAG 2.2 AA conformant' — it is about theme colour/perceivability, not whole-product conformance, and it is a target rather than an audited conformance statement. A VPAT is still the right artifact for a conformance assertion.

contradictions.lane_asserts: Freeze is offered in the column header menu of all columns.
contradictions.source_actually_says: The same tree-table page says both 'The Freeze/Unfreeze option is provided in the column header menu of all columns' (Freeze Columns section) AND 'For the tree column, the column header menu can contain the menu item Freeze and a Filter field. For all other columns, only the free text filter is available.' (Column Header Menu section).
contradictions.why_it_matters: SAP's page contradicts itself on whether Freeze is available on every column or only the tree column. The record drives an implementation decision ('expose freeze from the column header menu'). Resolve against the SAPUI5 API (sap.ui.table.Table property enableColumnFreeze) before building, rather than treating either sentence as settled.

contradictions.lane_asserts: Column position is changed with Ctrl plus arrow keys.
contradictions.source_actually_says: Tree-table 'Rearrange Columns' section: 'the focused column header can be moved by one position to the corresponding direction with Ctrl+Left / Ctrl+Right.' But the tree-table 'Column Header' component section says the same operation uses 'Shift+Left / Shift+Right' — which is also the documented RESIZE chord, making that reading self-defeating.
contradictions.why_it_matters: The record's stated value is 'concrete keybindings to implement in the WBS grid header'. The grid-table and analytical-table pages both independently say Ctrl+Left/Ctrl+Right for reorder and Shift+Left/Shift+Right for resize, so implement Ctrl for reorder; but do not present the tree-table page as an unambiguous single source for it.

unreachable_pages: /v1-148/discover/sap-design-system/product-standards/accessibility-in-sap-fiori (5 records: R09-061, 063, 064, 065, 069) — navigation failed/404 on ~6 attempts across 3 tabs; v1-136 and v1-120 equivalents also failed
/v1-148/foundations/interaction/keyboard-support (1 record: R09-060) — navigation failed on 5 attempts; absent from the interaction foundations link index
/v1-148/foundations/interaction/screen-reader (1 record: R09-066) — returns SAP's own 404 body; absent from the interaction foundations link index
summary.lane_quality_assessment: R09 is a strong lane. 100 of 107 evidence quotes matched the live Tier-1 sources verbatim, the sourcing is almost entirely first-party, and the IP discipline around theme colour values was respected. The three defects are all directionally the same: a correct SAP sentence is restated with a qualifier removed, hardening a soft guideline into a constraint (R09-008, R09-015, R09-070). The single most consequential is R09-008. The accessibility cluster (7 records) could not be re-fetched and must not be quoted as verified, though the lane's own gap note on that cluster turns out to be too pessimistic — see contradictions[0).
